author_or_org: Jessica Diaz, Joaquin Gayoso, Andrea Cimminio, Jorge Perez (arXiv)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper reports an industry productivity paradox in which individual developer productivity rises while team throughput, review capacity, and stability degrade because team-scale software engineering discipline is neglected.
claims.quote: However, industry reports a productivity paradox: as individual productivity increases, team throughput, review capacity, and stability degrade because team-scale software engineering discipline is neglected.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper's proposed intent artifact is the specification, described as the contract substrate between humans and agents within a socio-technical model of SDD.
claims.quote: Using a comparative characterization of the paradigm progression as conceptual framing, the article presents (i) a socio-technical model of SDD in which specifications act as the contract substrate between humans and agents; (ii) an operational characterization of the harness, distinguishing the technical harness around the agent from the methodological harness around the team, with worked examples; and (iii) a typology of five human--agent interaction patterns through which the human role is redefined.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Review capacity is explicitly named as a team-scale capacity that degrades under the AI productivity paradox.
claims.quote: However, industry reports a productivity paradox: as individual productivity increases, team throughput, review capacity, and stability degrade because team-scale software engineering discipline is neglected.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The paper proposes a methodological harness around the team and a typology of five human-agent interaction patterns through which the human role is redefined.
claims.quote: Using a comparative characterization of the paradigm progression as conceptual framing, the article presents (i) a socio-technical model of SDD in which specifications act as the contract substrate between humans and agents; (ii) an operational characterization of the harness, distinguishing the technical harness around the agent from the methodological harness around the team, with worked examples; and (iii) a typology of five human--agent interaction patterns through which the human role is redefined.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper is a conceptual analysis based predominantly on gray literature because peer-reviewed evidence and a shared academic-industrial vocabulary are not yet established.
claims.quote: We conducted a conceptual analysis drawing predominantly on gray literature, including ASE vision and roadmap papers, practitioner reports, talks, and tooling, because peer-reviewed evidence and a shared academic-industrial vocabulary are not yet established.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The paper presents its work as a first step rather than a validated theory and calls for future empirical validation.
claims.quote: Given the immaturity of the evidence base, this work is presented as a first step toward academic-industrial consensus rather than a validated theory, and outlines a research agenda for future empirical validation.
